Diagnosis is confident but no patch could be staged/submitted: no staging tool is exposed in this environment, so I cannot produce a validated public-green candidate. Root cause: ConstTag.js builds `create_derived(context.state, b.thunk(init))` for `{@const x = await ...}`. When the init contains an AwaitExpression, the emitted thunk arrow is not async, so the client output becomes `$.derived(() => await Promise.resolve(5))` — a non-async function containing await — which fails at parse time ('await isn't allowed in non-async function'). The fix (hyp 1/2, unverified) is to make ConstTag detect an await in the init (node.metadata.expression.contains_await) and emit an async derived thunk consistent with how $derived-with-await is compiled, plus matching SSR handling; this was never staged or evaluated, so correctness (including hydrate mode) is unconfirmed.

The diagnosis is complete and a concrete fix is identified, but this session exposes no staging/patch tool, so I cannot stage a candidate within the remaining budget. Root cause: ConstTag.js (packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/client/visitors/ConstTag.js, lines ~22-26 and ~55-70) always wraps the @const initializer in create_derived(context.state, b.thunk(init)), which compiles to $.derived(() => await ...) — a bare await inside a non-async arrow, producing the rollup parse error 'await isn't allowed in non-async function'. The required fix (matching VariableDeclaration.js's $derived handling, lines 200-222): (1) in analysis, register @const initial CallExpressions containing await in analysis.async_deriveds (e.g. in CallExpression.js ~line 248, or when analyzing ConstTag), and (2) in ConstTag.js, when the init is an async derived, emit b.call('$.async_derived', b.thunk(init, true)) wrapped as b.call(b.await(b.call('$.save', call))) instead of the plain derived thunk (for both the Identifier and destructuring branches, using the async arrow thunk so await is legal). This mirrors the proven working pattern for $derived and should make the public holdout test (text '5' in client and hydrate modes) pass while preserving non-async @const behavior.
